key_insight: The paper builds a fully algebraic multiscale coarse space for two-level overlapping Schwarz preconditioners that preserves robustness for highly heterogeneous elliptic and elasticity problems.
engineering_relevance: It offers a matrix-only route to scalable domain decomposition preconditioners, reducing coarse problem size while maintaining strong performance on difficult multiscale mechanics and diffusion cases.
method: Constructs coarse basis functions by solving algebraic reduced boundary condition (RBC) problems on subdomain interfaces.
Uses energy-minimizing extensions of interface solutions so coefficient variation is encoded in the coarse space.
Extends the framework to unstructured decompositions and linear elasticity via an energy-minimizing formulation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports contrast-independent iteration counts for high-coefficient inclusions, and in 3D log-normal diffusion the method matches GDSW iteration counts while solving a coarse problem about 10× smaller.
watch_item: The fully algebraic elasticity variant drops rotational rigid-body basis functions, so robustness may depend on problem class and decomposition details.
paper_title: An algebraic multiscale framework for two-level overlapping Schwarz preconditioners
